# Task Cleanup

Verify, review once, write the short PR body, merge, and close the ticket. Held to the 1:1 budget (owner decision 2026-10-02, IAN-568): the tail of a task never takes longer than the task, except for the R-109 security review.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the task-cleanup skill to verify and close out this work."

## Who does what

The main session runs the verification gate, the review, the PR body, the merge, and every tracker write as direct MCP calls (IAN-345). Only on a Complex or Saga task may a background `haiku` or `sonnet` subagent write multi-file bookkeeping (product docs, the PR body, the handoff); it edits files and never commits or writes to the tracker.

## Step 1: What shipped

```bash
bash ~/.claude/skills/task-cleanup/scripts/scan.sh [--range <a>..<b>]
```

The scan answers from the diff whether user-facing behavior, components, endpoints, query parameters, a spec or plan, or a feature branch are involved, and prints the ledger's tier. A surface it cannot see is still yours to name.

## Step 2: Required actions

Run only the actions that apply.

**Verification gate.** The project's test, build, and lint commands pass before any merge (R-509).

**Product docs, at feature completion only** (R-607, R-608, R-508; owner decision 2026-10-02, IAN-568, decision 5). When this task completes a user-facing feature, update the docs once, in this PR, not on every push:

- `docs/feature-list/features.md`: the feature's row set to **Complete** or **Partial** with the gap named, and the `Last updated:` line rewritten.
- `docs/user-stories/<area>.md`: the story's shipped criteria ticked, and its `**E2E test:**` line naming the real spec under `e2e/`; a new flow gets a new `US-<AREA>-NNN` story.
- `docs/stack.md` and `docs/observability.md`: an entry for each dependency added, removed, or upgraded across a major version, and a row for each analytics event, log event, or error code added, renamed, or removed.
- `README.md`: when setup, structure, or a user-facing feature changed.

Skip a document the repository opts out of in `.enforce.json` (`"productDocs": false`, `"stackDoc": false`, `"observabilityDoc": false`). A shipped spec and plan are deleted; a partly shipped one keeps updated checkboxes. `docs/query-params.md` changes with any new query parameter.

**Trivial tier.** Open the PR and merge on green CI: no ticket, no PR document, and no R-517 review (the guard reads the exemption from the task-tier ledger for the PR's head branch). Done.

**Ticket.** When no ticket exists yet, open it now through `/ticket-lifecycle`, at the latest when the draft PR opens (R-605), and add `Refs: <KEY>` to the PR body.

**PR body.** Standard-risk PR, the short template:

```
## Summary
<what changed and why, in two or three sentences>

## Testing
<the tests added or changed, and what they prove>

## Codex review
<the section below>
```

A high-risk PR adds `## Decisions` (chosen versus the alternative, and why) and `## Reflection` (what went well, what to change).

**Pre-merge review (R-517).** Every PR above trivial gets one fresh-context review after the last bookkeeping commit:

1. Fill `~/.claude/prompts/codex-pr-review-prompt.md` with the base and head, the spec path or "none", the requirement text, the touched convention files, and the diff (generated trees and lock files excluded).
2. Dispatch the read-only `pr-reviewer` agent on `sonnet` with it, for every PR, high-risk and security-touching ones included. Codex or `opus`/`fable` only when the owner opts in; Codex runs as `codex exec -s read-only ... </dev/null > <log> 2>&1` in the background, polled through the log, and falls back to an `opus` subagent.
3. **Review rounds.** One round per PR. Run a second round only when round one finds a HIGH. Fix each valid finding as an ordinary commit carrying a test that fails without it, never as a full TDD slice. A LOW left after the last round becomes a ticket (`finding.sh add "<what>" --kind <kind> --value low`) answered in the PR with its key. A HIGH or MEDIUM still blocks the merge. A security finding of any severity is fixed or waived by the owner, never ticketed (R-109).
4. Write the section with three labelled lines and a findings table:

   ```
   ## Codex review
   - reviewer: Claude subagent (sonnet)
   - model: claude-sonnet-5
   - range: <base sha>..<head sha>

   | # | Round | Severity | Finding | Disposition |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | 1 | r1 | MEDIUM | <finding> | fixed abc1234 |
   | 2 | r1 | LOW | <finding> | ticketed IAN-123 |
   ```

   The `range` head must be the PR head, or an ancestor of it when every later commit is a clean base merge or is named in this table in a cell starting with `fixed` (`fixed <sha>`); a plain bullet list of fixes does not count, and any other later commit means re-running the review. The R-109 `## Security review` has no such tail: when fixes land after it, its range must end at the commit that carries the fixes (the artefact commit). The section keeps the heading "Codex review" whichever reviewer ran, and there is exactly one.

**Merge** (R-514). The owner reads and merges a security-touching PR (R-109) or one `build-lane.sh classify` classes guarded. Every other PR follows its plan's `**Merge mode:**` line, or build-fast's `mergeMode`: merge on green CI and a passed review through the guard's confirmation, or hand it to the owner. `gh pr merge <n> --squash --delete-branch --repo <owner/repo>`, then confirm the commit is on `main`. A `bundle` PR (2 to 5 small related tickets, never deletion, security, sync, or migration) rebase-merges. Remove a worktree after its merge.

**Findings.** `finding.sh open` lists findings still owed a ticket; open them or tell the owner, then `finding.sh clear`.

**Close the ticket** (R-606), after the merge: `done`, `completed_at`, `actual_minutes` (working time from the transcript's first timestamp, never the calendar gap), `risk`, and `pr_link`; `findings_by_round`, `escaped_bugs`, and the estimate ratios only when cheap. Abandoned work closes as `dropped` with the reason.

**Handoff, once per session** (R-601, R-602). Only at session end, and only when work is left open: write `docs/session-handoff/session-handoff.md` (under 8 KB: last commit, production state, session metrics from `bash ~/.claude/hooks/session-metrics.sh`, what shipped, pending work with open ticket keys, next steps) and commit it on the work PR's branch before its review. A handoff never gets a PR of its own.

## Step 3: Report

Output one short table of what ran (gate, docs, review, merge, ticket, handoff) with each outcome, then `bash ~/.claude/skills/task-start/scripts/task-tier.sh clear`.

## Common Mistakes

- Updating product docs on every push instead of once at feature completion.
- Running a second review round when round one found no HIGH.
- Recording fixes as a bullet list instead of `fixed <sha>` cells in the findings table.
- Opening a separate PR for the handoff.
- Writing the calendar gap as `actual_minutes`.

## Integration

- **Paired with:** task-start
- **Calls:** ticket-lifecycle (`open` when missing, then `close`)
- **Uses:** `prompts/codex-pr-review-prompt.md` (R-517)
